headline: DISCOVERY CONFIRMS 3.70 MOZ AT PAMOUR — 3.05 g/t Over 30m in Central Pit; 4km Strike Traced to 700m Depth (TSX: DSV)
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV) released assay results from 47 holes (11,003m) at the Pamour Mine in Ontario, confirming a large-scale open-pit resource of 64.8 million tonnes at 1.30 g/t gold (2.70 Moz indicated) plus 23.3 million tonnes at 1.34 g/t gold (1.00 Moz inferred) — 3.70 Moz total — across a mineralized system traced over 4.0 km of strike and 300 to 700 metres of depth that remains open. Standout intercepts in the latest batch include 3.05 g/t over 30.0m and 8.04 g/t over 6.5m in the Central Pit, and a bonanza-grade hit of 27.00 g/t over 1.0m in the Pamour West high-grade zone, all within the company's 255,000–285,000m 2026 exploration program — one of the largest in Timmins camp history.

headline: SILVER X EXPANDS RED SILVER DRILL 5.5X TO 6,650M — Triggered by 735 g/t Ag Over 65m Channel; Peru Underground Program Underway (CVE: AGX)
snippet: Silver X Mining Corp. (CVE: AGX) announced that underground diamond drilling is now underway at the Red Silver (María Luz sector) target within its flagship Nueva Recuperada Project in Huancavelica, Peru — with the program expanded from the initial 1,200-metre plan to 6,650 metres after high-grade channel sampling returned 735 g/t silver over 65 metres of strike length and 649 g/t Ag over 40 metres. Drilling is conducted from existing underground workings approximately 8 km from the company's Nueva Recuperada processing plant, with a dual objective of growing the current NI 43-101 mineral resource and upgrading inferred ounces to measured and indicated categories.

headline: GOLD ABOVE $4,150 AS HOUTHI BLOCKS BAB EL-MANDEB, U.S. STRIKES IRAN FOR 11TH NIGHT — Brent at $94; Seven Tankers Turn Around
snippet: Gold pushed above $4,150 per ounce on Wednesday — its highest level in two weeks — as Middle East escalation added a fresh geopolitical bid on top of Tuesday's FOMC-driven rally: Iran-backed Houthi rebels declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and attacked ships near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, causing at least seven crude oil tankers to reverse course in the Red Sea, while the U.S. military completed an eleventh night of airstrikes against Iran with no ceasefire in sight. Brent crude climbed to $93–94 per barrel on fears of twin chokepoint disruptions at both Bab el-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz, with silver also recovering above $59 per ounce as the dual threat of higher inflation and geopolitical uncertainty reinforced the precious metals safe-haven bid.

headline: IEA WARNS 20% OF COPPER AT RISK: Chile Acid Crisis Deepens as China Bans Exports and Middle East War Cuts Sulfur Supply
snippet: Chile's copper sector is facing a critical sulphuric acid shortage after China stopped exporting the feedstock to South America for the first time since July 2023, and Middle East fighting has disrupted seaborne sulfur flows — nearly half of global supply comes from the region — sending spot acid prices roughly double year-over-year. BHP's non-integrated operations are among the most exposed: Escondida output fell 17.6% and Spence dropped 34.4% in Q1, while the IEA has warned that up to 20% of global copper mine production could be affected if the shortfall persists, with codelco holding an advantage through integrated smelter acid recovery that independents like BHP and Antofagasta lack.

headline: TANZANIA CENTRAL BANK BUYS 28 TONNES OF GOLD IN 18 MONTHS — $3.68B Reserve Build Joins EM Central Bank Gold Wave
snippet: Bank of Tanzania Governor Emmanuel Tutuba announced the country has increased its gold holdings by 28 tonnes over the past 18 months, valued at approximately $3.68 billion at current prices, after regulations imposed in June 2025 required large-scale miners operating in Tanzania to sell at least 20% of production locally and exporters to sell 20% directly to the central bank. Tanzania now holds around $6 billion in total reserves — approximately 4.3 months of import cover — with the gold-buying program aimed at supporting the Tanzanian shilling, diversifying away from dollar-denominated assets, and strengthening financial-sector stability in one of Africa's top-10 gold-producing nations.

headline: SILVER INSTITUTE: GOLD:SILVER RATIO AT 69.2:1 — Near 50-Year Top; Statistical Analysis Shows Mean Reversion to 60:1 Inevitable
snippet: The Silver Institute released a Market Trend Report on July 22 showing the gold-to-silver ratio stands at 69.2:1 — near the top of its 50-year historical range — and that statistical analysis of data from January 1970 through May 2026 confirms the ratio is not a random walk but a mean-reverting series with a long-run equilibrium of just under 60:1. The report notes that the price correlation between gold and silver has actually strengthened over the past two decades as both markets have become increasingly financialized, suggesting that silver's current discount to gold relative to historical norms represents an opportunity for investors who can tolerate the metal's higher volatility and are positioned ahead of a ratio reversion.

headline: NdPr MAGNET METALS HIT 2026 HIGH — Neodymium +21% to $145.86/Kg, Praseodymium +25% to $152.86/Kg; EV and Wind Turbine Deficit Persists
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) rare earth prices reached new 2026 highs in July, with neodymium oxide climbing to $145.86 per kilogram in Northeast Asia (up 21.4% from June) and praseodymium at $152.86 per kilogram (up 24.6%), driven by stringent production quota enforcement and environmental compliance curtailments at Chinese rare earth mining and separation facilities. The NdPr alloy — the primary commercial product used in permanent magnets for EV motors and direct-drive wind turbines — reached approximately $133/kg as of early July, a new 2026 high reflecting a second consecutive year of structural supply deficit as demand from global EV and clean energy buildouts continues to outpace mining output from both China and the nascent Western supply chain.

headline: JEFFERIES: BRENT AT $94 PUTS OPEN-PIT GOLD MINER H2 COSTS AT RISK — Budgets Set at $70; Oil Up 45% Over Plan Since Iran War
snippet: Jefferies has warned that elevated gold prices alone will not offset the cost pressures facing open-pit gold miners if Brent crude — which hit $94.13 per barrel on July 22 — holds at current levels through H2 2026, noting that most producers built 2026 budgets around $70 per barrel and are now running approximately 45% over their energy cost assumptions since Middle East conflict escalated in late February. Diesel typically accounts for 15–25% of all-in sustaining costs at large open-pit operations, and Jefferies calculates that a 10% increase in oil prices raises average AISC by about $10 per ounce — implying total H2 cost headwinds of $35–$45/oz that could translate into as much as a 9% cost increase for the most fuel-exposed operators in Africa and Latin America.

headline: RENFORTH VICTORIA Ni/Cu/Co: VISUAL MINERALIZATION IN BOTH UNDERCUT HOLES — Quebec Battery Metals Deposit Tested Below Existing Resource (CSE: RFR)
snippet: Renforth Resources Inc. (CSE: RFR) updated on its ongoing drill program at the wholly owned Victoria Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Open Pit Polymetallic deposit between Cadillac and Malartic, Quebec, where two undercut holes drilled at 45 and 65 degrees into the first target area both encountered visual mineralization — the program's initial results since establishing an initial mineral resource estimate. The undercut holes target continuity below prior positive intercepts including 74.55 metres at 0.14% nickel and 10.5 metres at 0.52% copper, in the first drill campaign explicitly designed to test whether the Victoria deposit's battery metal package — nickel, cobalt, and copper — extends meaningfully below the current resource envelope.
